cited.finding: Anterior insula is associated with feelings of guilt
cited.anchor: Several brain regions have been associated with the feeling of guilt: the anterior insula (aIns) (Bastin et al., 2016; Lamm & Singer, 2010; Piretti et al., 2023)

cited.finding: A multivariate neural guilt-related brain signature (GRBS) can be identified across studies
cited.anchor: A recent study by Yu and colleagues re-analysed the results of two previous neuroimaging studies of guilt and obtained a neural multivariate guilt-related brain signature (guilt-related brain signature, GRBS) (Yu et al., 2020).

cited.finding: People display responsibility aversion in group decisions; medial prefrontal cortex, anterior insula and temporo-parietal junction are involved in seeking or avoiding responsibility
cited.anchor: One landmark study reported on the mechanisms involved in seeking or avoiding responsibility in decisions affecting a group of individuals, and reported involvement of medial prefrontal cortex, aIns and temporo-parietal junction (Edelson et al., 2018).

cited.finding: Bilateral ventral striatum shows greater response when choosing risky vs safe options
cited.anchor: which replicates previous findings (Cui et al., 2022; Preuschoff et al., 2006)

cited.finding: Being responsible for somebody else's payoffs increases risk aversion
cited.anchor: At least two studies reported that being responsible for somebody else's payoffs increases risk aversion (Fareri et al., 2022; Pahlke et al., 2015).

cited.finding: Meta-analysis found no difference in risk preferences when choosing for oneself vs. for others
cited.anchor: Indeed, recent large meta-analyses comparing risky choices for oneself vs. for others report either no difference in risk preferences (Batteux et al., 2019)
